steps.title: Open branch settings
steps.instruction: Open erezlev13/skills → Settings → Branches. You need repository administration access.
steps.expected: The branch protection section is visible.
steps.detail: This guide records your progress only. It does not change GitHub settings. If the option is unavailable, use My screen is different; availability can depend on repository visibility and your GitHub plan.

steps.title: Check for an existing rule
steps.instruction: Is there already a classic branch protection rule for main?

choices.label: Yes, a rule for main exists

steps.title: Edit the main rule
steps.instruction: Click Edit beside the existing rule for main. Preserve any protections already enabled.
steps.expected: The rule editor shows main as the branch name pattern.

steps.title: Create a rule for main
steps.instruction: Click Add classic branch protection rule. Set Branch name pattern to main.

steps.title: Require a pull request
steps.instruction: Enable Require a pull request before merging. For a new solo-owner rule, leave Require approvals off so you can merge your own PRs. If editing an existing rule, preserve any approval requirement unless you intend to change it.
steps.expected: Require a pull request before merging is checked.

steps.title: Apply protection to administrators
steps.instruction: Enable Do not allow bypassing the above settings. Keep Allow force pushes and Allow deletions off. Do not add actors allowed to bypass required pull requests.
steps.expected: The rule applies to administrators as well as other contributors.

steps.title: Save and check the rule
steps.instruction: Click Create or Save changes. Reopen the saved rule and confirm that it targets main, requires a pull request, and prevents bypassing. Click Done only after you have checked the saved settings.
steps.expected: The saved protection rule appears for main with the intended settings.
